finding: Feature-level fusion achieved the lowest out-of-fold MAE among all evaluated models.
Feature-level fusion improved over the strongest structured-only CatBoost model.
The fusion advantage was consistent in most folds but was not conventionally statistically significant.
evidence: Fusion won 4/5 folds; paired t-test p=0.0991; Wilcoxon p=0.1250; Cohen's dz=0.957.

finding: Review text was the most influential information group in the final fusion framework.
evidence: Removing review text increased MAE by 5.90%.

finding: Category information made the second-largest feature-group contribution.
Price-related information contributed meaningful additional predictive signal.
evidence: Removing price features increased MAE by 3.21%.

finding: Engagement variables contributed the least among the tested structured feature groups.
evidence: Removing engagement features increased MAE by 0.73%.

finding: Global text explanations were directionally coherent with product-review sentiment.
evidence: Positive terms included excellent, awesome, easy, good quality and perfect; negative terms included not, bad, poor, waste of and not working.

finding: Local OOF explanations were numerically reproducible within the predefined reconstruction tolerance.
evidence: 3/3 representative cases passed; maximum absolute reconstruction difference=0.00002539.
